questions.stem: Which of the following is transmitted by all the components of blood?

Malaria

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a marker for Gastrointestinal stromal tumors?
questions.solutionHtml:
NRG-1
  • 75% of all GISTs have oncogenic, gain-of- function mutations in the receptor tyrosine kinase KIT. While 8% of GISTs have activating mutations in platelet-derived growth factor receptor α (PDGFRA).
  • Succinate dehydrogenase (SDH)-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is a subset of wild-type GIST that constitutes approximately 10% of gastric GISTs

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect regarding myelodysplastic syndrome?

options.label: B
options.text: Treatment induced MDS is not dependent on age

questions.solutionHtml:
More commonly seen in females
  • Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) are a heterogeneous group of acquired clonal stem cell disorders affecting stem cells

MDS is characterized by:

  • Progressive cytopenias
  • Dysplasia in one or more cell lines
  • Ineffective hematopoiesis
  • Risk of development of AML.

Classification

Idiopathic or primary MDS

  • Secondary/therapy-related MDS (t-MDS):Complication of previous cytotoxic drug or radiation therapy.

WHO classification

  • MDS with single lineage dysplasia
  • MDS with ring sideroblasts
    • MDS with ring sideroblasts and single lineage dysplasia
    • MDS with ring sideroblasts and multilineage dysplasia
  • MDS with multilineage dysplasia
  • MDS with excess blasts
  • MDS with isolated del(5q)
  • MDS, unclassifiable

Clinical features

Elderly above 60 years

  • Slightly more common in males
  • Symptoms are due to cytopenias
  • About 10%–40% of MDS patients progress to AML

Laboratory findings

Peripheral smear: Cytopenias in the peripheral blood

  • RBCs: Mild to moderate degree of macrocytic or dimorphic anemia.
  • WBCs: Normal or low total leukocyte count.
  • Platelets: Variable thrombocytopenia, large hypogranular or giant platelet
  • Bone marrow findings
  • Dysplasia of all nonlymphoid lineages (erythroid, granulocytic, monocytic and megakaryocytic) associated with cytopenias.

Cellularity: Hypercellular.

  • Erythropoiesis: Dysplastic changes in erythroid precursors with megaloblastoid change and presence of ringed sideroblasts in iron stain.
  • Myelopoiesis: Hyperplasia with dysgranulopoiesis.
  • Megakaryopoiesis: Dysmegakaryopoiesis—pawn ball megakaryocytes.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 620

questions.stem: Which of the following about Hodgkin's lymphoma is not true?

options.label: A
options.text: Waldeyer's ring is the most common site to be involved

options.label: B
options.text: RS cells are immunopositive for CD30 and PAX5

options.label: C
options.text: RS Cells are of B cell origin

options.label: D
options.text: Nodular sclerosis is the most commonly presents as a mediastinal mass

questions.answerText: Waldeyer's ring is the most common site to be involved
questions.solutionHtml:
Waldeyer's ring is the most common site to be involved
  • Reed-Sternberg cells are of B cell origin and show immunopositivity for PAX 5, CD 15 and CD 30.
  • Nodular sclerosis variants of Hodgkin’s lymphoma have high propensity to involve cervical and mediastinal lymph nodes. These are the correct statements.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 611

questions.stem: Which of the following is the nuclear neuroendocrine immunohistochemical marker?
